questions: Should the function handle groups that are not separated by exactly one space, e.g., multiple spaces or tabs?
If the input string contains no spaces, should it be treated as a single group or as zero groups?
Should empty strings resulting from leading/trailing spaces be ignored or cause an error?
If a group has mismatched parentheses (e.g., more closes than opens), should the function raise an error, return a negative depth, or continue processing?
Are characters other than '(' and ')' allowed within a group, and if so, should they be ignored, raise an error, or affect depth?
Should the function return an empty list for an empty input string, or raise an error?
If a group is empty (e.g., consecutive spaces producing an empty substring), should it be skipped or produce a depth of 0?
Should the depth be counted as the maximum number of open parentheses at any point, or the maximum nesting level defined differently (e.g., counting pairs)?
